'''Richard Henry Jude''' (1853 – 1 June 1924) was an English [[mathematician]], physicist and [[animal rights]] campaigner.

==Career==

Jude was born in [[Camberwell]] and was educated at [[King's College London]] where he won a mathematics scholarship.<ref name="Newcastle">{{cite news|url=https://www.findmypast.co.uk/image-viewer?issue=BL%2F0000569%2F19180430&page=6|title=Presentation to Dr R. H. Jude|newspaper=The Newcastle Daily Journal|date=April 30, 1918|page=6|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 1872 he received honours from [[University of London]] and qualified B.Sc with first-class honours in mathematics.<ref name="Newcastle"/> In 1878, he obtained a [[Doctor of Science]] degree in organic chemistry from the University of London and in 1880 proceeded to a [[Master of Arts]] degree at [[Cambridge University]].<ref name="Newcastle"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.findmypast.co.uk/image-viewer?issue=BL%2F0005588%2F18780720&page=6|title=Teston|newspaper=The Maidstone and Kent Country Standard |date=July 20, 1878|page=6|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

He was appointed lecturer in mathematics and science at [[Northumbria University|Rutherford College]] in 1882 where he remained until his retirement in 1917.<ref name="Newcastle"/> He was Head of the Physical and Mathematical Departments.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.findmypast.co.uk/image-viewer?issue=BL%2F9900012%2F19011201&page=5|title=Mathematics and Physics|newspaper=The Educational Times |date=February 1, 1901|page=43|url-access=subscription}}</ref> As a teacher he was credited with playing a prominent role in the higher education of young [[engineer]]s.<ref name="Nature">{{cite journal |author= Lawson, Robert W.| date=1924 |title=Dr. R. H. Jude |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/114286a0 |journal=Nature |volume=114 |issue= |pages=286 |doi=10.1038/114286a0|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He authored four physics textbooks which were translated into Russian and invented new physics apparatus which were patented.<ref name="Newcastle"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.findmypast.co.uk/image-viewer?issue=BL%2F0001714%2F19240603&page=2|title=Death at Eltham of Former Lecturer at Rutherford College|newspaper=North Mail and Newcastle Chronicle |date=June 3, 1924|page=2|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==Animal rights==

Jude was an advocate of animal rights and served on the provisional committee of the [[Humanitarian League]] in 1891.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.findmypast.co.uk/image-viewer?issue=BL%2F0001634%2F18910401&page=8|title=The Humanitarian League|newspaper=The Newcastle Daily Chronicle |date=April 1, 1891|page=8|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 1891, Jude authored a paper for the National Cat Club on "Feline Intelligence".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.findmypast.co.uk/image-viewer?issue=BL%2F0006349%2F18910319&page=11|title=Club and Society Notices|newspaper=Fur and Feather |date=March 19, 1891|page=171|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 1892, he authored a pamphlet for the Humanitarian League criticizing the cruelty of [[rabbit coursing]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.findmypast.co.uk/image-viewer?issue=BL%2F0000098%2F18921116&page=5|title=The Humanitarian League and its Aims: An Interview with H. S. Salt|newspaper=Pall Mall Gazette |date=November 16, 1892|page=5|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.findmypast.co.uk/image-viewer?issue=BL%2F0003358%2F18930305&page=7|title=Waifs and Strays|newspaper=The Weekly |date=March 5, 1893|page=7|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Jude wrote that the rabbits "often half-starved, and with their legs broken, are huddled together in a sack, with no more consideration than if they were so many bundles of wood" and how they were turned loose to be chased by greyhounds and other dogs to be bitten to death or [[Disembowelment|disembowelled]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.findmypast.co.uk/image-viewer?issue=BL%2F0000668%2F19060807&page=4|title=The Quality of Mercy|newspaper=Birmingham Gazette and Express |date=August 7, 1906|page=4|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Jude was an honorary correspondent of the [[Victoria Street Society for the Protection of Animals from Vivisection]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.findmypast.co.uk/image-viewer?issue=BL%2F0000726%2F18921007&page=3|title=The Church Congress and Vivisection|newspaper=The Evening Chronicle |date=October 7, 1892|page=3|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He was a speaker at the 1892 annual meeting of the [[London Anti-Vivisection Society]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.findmypast.co.uk/image-viewer?issue=BL%2F0001724%2F18920607&page=8|title=London Anti-Vivisection Society|newspaper=Eastern Daily Press |date=June 7, 1892|page=8|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 1897, he contributed an article to [[Henry S. Salt]]'s ''Cruelties of Civilization: A Programme of Humane Reform''.<ref name="Sheffield">{{cite news|url=https://www.findmypast.co.uk/image-viewer?issue=BL%2F0000181%2F18950410&page=2|title=Bellamy Library|newspaper=The Sheffield and Rotherham Independent |date=April 10, 1895|page=2|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==Death==

Jude towards the end of his life had [[diabetes]] and was deaf and blind.<ref name="Nature"/> He died at [[Eltham]] on 1 June 1924, aged 71.<ref name="Nature"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.findmypast.co.uk/image-viewer?issue=BL%2F0000901%2F19240604&page=5|title=Death of Dr R. H. Jude|newspaper=Huddersfield Daily Examiner |date=June 4, 1924|page=5|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He was buried at Borough Green Baptist Cemetery.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.findmypast.co.uk/image-viewer?issue=BL%2F0005836%2F19240607&page=2|title=The Week's Deaths|newspaper=Bromley Guide and Avertiser |date=June 7, 1924|page=2|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In spite of his ill health in his last years, an obituary in the ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' journal noted that he "retained to the end a brave fortitude in his outlook, an active and a clear mentality, and his letters rarely lacked in that spark of dry humour so characteristic of him in earlier years".<ref name="Nature"/>
